School vocabulary
Fill up
Eat until you are no longer hungry — Llenarse / saciarse.
The children filled up on bread.
Become full of people — Llenarse.
The hall filled up quickly.
School vocabulary
Put together
Organise ideas or a plan to present them — Elaborar / preparar.
She put together a proposal overnight.
Place things close to each other — Juntar / acercar.
Put the two tables together.
School vocabulary
Call back
Ask someone to return after they have left — Hacer volver / llamar de nuevo.
The manager called her back for a second interview.
School vocabulary
Hurry up
Make something happen faster — Acelerar / meter prisa a.
Can you hurry the order up?
School vocabulary
Get in
Receive a delivery, of a shop — Recibir / llegarle a uno.
The shop got the new models in yesterday.
Find the time for an activity — Sacar tiempo para / colar.
I got a swim in before work.
School vocabulary
Take out
Withdraw money — Sacar / retirar.
He took out two hundred euros.
Take someone somewhere enjoyable — Invitar a salir / llevar.
They took us out to dinner.
School vocabulary
Put back
Delay something to a later date — Aplazar / retrasar.
The opening was put back to May.
Slow down a project — Retrasar.
The storm put the work back by weeks.
School vocabulary
Put down
Criticise someone and make them feel small — Menospreciar / humillar.
He is always putting his brother down.
Pay part of the cost in advance — Dar de entrada.
We put down ten per cent on the flat.
School vocabulary
Get on
Mount an animal or bicycle — Subirse a / montar en.
She got on the horse easily.
Carry on with what you were doing — Seguir / continuar.
Let me get on with my work.
School vocabulary
Get off
Be let off with little or no punishment — Librarse / salir bien parado.
He got off with a warning.
Have time away from work — Librar / tener libre.
I get Friday off.
School vocabulary
Move out
Take someone's belongings out of a place — Sacar / desalojar.
They moved the tenants out in a day.
School vocabulary
Go up
Rise in price or level — Subir / aumentar.
Rents have gone up again.
Extend as far as a point — Llegar hasta.
The path goes up to the lake.
School vocabulary
Hand in
Give notice that you are leaving a job — Presentar / entregar.
She handed in her resignation.
Give something up to someone in authority — Entregar.
All phones must be handed in.
School vocabulary
Turn in
Report someone to the police — Denunciar / entregar.
His own brother turned him in.
Go to bed — Irse a la cama / acostarse.
I'm tired; I think I'll turn in.
School vocabulary
Fill in
Tell someone what they have missed — Poner al corriente / informar.
Fill me in on the meeting.
Do someone else's job for a while — Sustituir / cubrir.
She filled in for the usual driver.
School vocabulary
Point out
Stress a piece of information — Señalar / hacer notar.
He pointed out that the shop was closed.
School vocabulary
Bring up
Raise a child — Criar / educar.
She was brought up by her grandmother.
Carry something up from below — Subir.
Could you bring the boxes up?
School vocabulary
Put off
Make someone lose interest or feel uneasy — Desanimar / echar para atrás.
His manner put me off at once.
School vocabulary
Deal with
Be about a subject, of a book or film — Tratar de / versar sobre.
The film deals with the war.
School vocabulary
Ask for
Behave so that trouble is deserved — Buscárselo.
Driving like that, he was asking for it.
School vocabulary
Get through
Finish something that takes effort — Terminar / acabar con.
I got through the report by midnight.
Make someone understand — Hacerse entender / llegar a.
I just can't get through to him.
School vocabulary
Check in
Hand over your luggage at an airport — Facturar.
We checked the bags in at nine.
Contact someone briefly to see how they are — Dar señales / pasarse a ver.
She checks in with her mother every day.
School vocabulary
Sign out
Borrow something and write your name for it — Llevarse firmando / registrar la salida de.
He signed out the projector.
